title: Shadow Traffic, Canary Rollout, and Progressive Deployment for LLMs

questions.question: What is the defining user-impact property of shadow traffic?
options: The candidate receives all traffic at 100% immediately
The baseline is deleted before comparison
Shadow mode bypasses cost and latency measurement
questions.explanation: Shadow mode compares candidate samples while the baseline remains the serving response, so candidate output has zero user exposure.

questions.question: Which cost value breaches the canary cost gate when BASELINE cost_per_req is $0.02?
questions.explanation: The gate is 1.2 × $0.02 = $0.024; a value above that, such as $0.030, breaches. Equality is not a breach because check_gates uses >.

questions.question: What is the first traffic stage in STAGES?
questions.explanation: The progressive sequence is [0.01, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00], so the first canary stage is 1%.

questions.question: What should happen to a cost_mult=1.25 rollout once the cost gate is exceeded?
options: It is promoted because cost is not an LLM gate
It silently changes the baseline cost
It retries the same stage until the noise disappears
questions.explanation: GATES allows only 1.2× cost; a 25% regression breaches, so rollout returns after printing HALT and the rollback action.

questions.question: What does PolicyEngine.rollback() do to the pinned digest and rollout percentage?
options: Pins the candidate and sets rollout to 100%
Keeps the candidate at the current percentage
Deletes both digests so no model can serve
questions.explanation: rollback optionally updates baselineDigest, sets pinnedDigest to that baseline, and resets rolloutPct=0 for an O(1) policy flip.

questions.question: When does shadowEvaluate set alert=true?
options: When one baseline cost is exactly zero
Only when candidate output text differs
questions.explanation: The policy builds reasons for meanCost > 30 or meanLat > 50; alert is true when at least one reason exists.
